symptom: `create agent … (Entity: M.E)` (and `create or modify`, and `alter agent … set Entity`) stored the agent's context entity as {"documentId":"","qualifiedName":"M.E"}; Studio Pro stores the entity's id there. A missing entity was not refused either.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_agenteditor_carry.go agentEntityRef, used by cmd_agenteditor_write.go (create) and cmd_agenteditor_alter.go (set Entity). Test: issue2289_agent_entity_docid_test.go
cause: A code comment asserted the documentId was an opaque Agent Editor-internal id filled at runtime, so the writer set only qualifiedName and a later carry (carryEntityRef) only patched over it when a stored id existed.
insight: **A JSON documentId inside a custom-blob document is whatever Studio Pro's element id is, even for a non-unit element.** For an entity it is the EntityImpl element's $ID, and mxcli's model.ID string for that element is already the same canonical GUID text Studio Pro writes (BSON binary in .NET order, JSON text canonical) — measured by matching AgentCommons' example agents' entity documentIds against `select Id from CATALOG.ENTITIES` on the Studio Pro-saved project. The cheap check that would have settled it a year earlier: grep a Studio Pro-saved project for the id. System entities have no $ID mxcli can see (System.Language stores 83d81a7b-…, not in the project), so they stay name-only with the stored id carried. Control: the model ref, already resolved, unchanged; a re-run of create or modify stays Unchanged.
